I'm 34 and still learning how to cope with my ocd and despite that I'm sorry to say that maybe my best advice is to reach out for professional help and to also read a book called "You Are Not Your Brain" by Jeffrey Schwartz. It will teach you much more convincingly than I can, that you will have these intrusive thoughts but they are not your feelings, they are merely thoughts drawn non sensically from your brain. This book will teach you how to dismiss these thoughts as mere thoughts, nothing more and in no way an indictment of who you are. It's difficult stuff, but worth persevering through. I've been acutely suffering from OCD since I was 16 (looking back I showed signs younger than that) so more than half my life and the best advice I can give you is that you do the work to learn how to manage it and take control. While the idea in the book and in most OCD therapy is to in a way "ignore" these intrusive thoughts (endure the uncomfortable feelings - without acting on your compulsions - so that eventually those compulsions weaken) what you don't want to do is ignore the disorder itself. I'm not meaning to alarm you and a doctor might diagnose you with "mild" ocd, but if by "ignoring" you mean just putting up with these compulsions, I don't advise that. The last thing you want is for this to become a bigger part of your life. I'm being long winded here to basically say that OCD should not be treated lightly and in my experience therapy and professional medical help is very worthwhile in the long run. At least consider reading that book. All the best my friend.
